classification.difficultyReason: Combine the number of globes, annual operating hours and one-time purchase cost into a model, solve for the hourly rate, then justify why doubling operating hours doubles only the running cost rather than the total.

content.prompt:
A clubhouse uses four long-life light globes for five hours every night of the year.
The purchase price of each light globe is $\$6.00$ and they each cost $d$ dollars per hour to run.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Write an equation for the total cost ($c$ dollars) of purchasing and running these four light globes for one year in terms of $d$.

answer.worked:
Each globe runs for $5\times365=1825$ hours in one year.

$$\begin{align*}c &= 4(6 + 1825d)\\c &= 24 + 7300d\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the value of $d$ (correct to three decimal places) if the total cost of purchasing and running these four light globes for one year is $\$250$.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}250 &= 24 + 7300d\\226 &= 7300d\\d &= \frac{226}{7300}\\d &\approx 0.031\end{align*}$$

The running cost is $\$0.031$ per globe per hour, correct to three decimal places.

children.label: c
children.prompt: If the use of the light globes increases to ten hours per night every night of the year, does the total cost double? Justify your answer with appropriate calculations.

answer.short: No. $c_{10}=4(6+3650d)=24+14600d$, whereas $2c_5=48+14600d$. Using the exact rate, the new total is $\$476$, not $\$500$.
answer.worked:
Each globe now runs for $10\times365=3650$ hours per year.

$$\begin{align*}c_{10} &= 4(6 + 3650d)\\c_{10} &= 24 + 14600d\\2c_5 &= 2(24 + 7300d)\\2c_5 &= 48 + 14600d\end{align*}$$

Using the exact rate from the previous part,

$$\begin{align*}c_{10} &= 24 + 14600\left(\frac{226}{7300}\right)\\c_{10} &= 476\end{align*}$$

No. The total becomes $\$476$, rather than $2\times\$250=\$500$, because the $\$24$ purchase cost is paid only once.
